soc.xg.label: Team xG for/against, shot quality, set-piece xG
soc.xg.mechanism: Shot-quality-weighted chance creation and prevention is a lower-noise estimate of underlying goal-scoring ability than realised goals, which carry large finishing and keeper variance.
soc.xg.rationale: Goals are rare and noisy; xG counts what a typical finisher would score from the same shot locations, so the sum over a sample converges to future goal rate faster than goals do. Subtle: xG models differ by provider, xG should be split open play / set piece / penalty, and raw averages are biased by schedule and game state. Using it unadjusted for opponent and venue rewards teams that padded stats against weak opposition.
soc.xg.measurement: Per team-match: open-play xG for/against excluding penalties and own goals, set-piece xG separately; exponentially time-weight (half-life ~ 8-12 league matches, tuned by CV), adjust for opponent and venue via a ridge/hierarchical regression (see soc.xg_adjusted_ratings), shrink to league mean by n/(n+k) with k ~ 8-10 matches.

soc.ratings.label: Elo/rating, opponent-adjusted goal models
soc.ratings.mechanism: A single latent strength per team updated from results and margins summarises opponent-adjusted quality, including across leagues when ratings are linked by European fixtures.
soc.ratings.rationale: Ratings convert a noisy result history into a calibrated prior for win/draw/loss and goal difference. Goal-margin Elo with a capped margin multiplier and home offset or a Dixon-Coles attack/defence fit are standard. Subtle: ratings lag squad changes, promoted clubs and mid-season managerial changes; cross-league comparability is only as good as the number of inter-league matches.
soc.ratings.measurement: Fit Dixon-Coles/Poisson attack-defence by weighted likelihood with exponential time decay (xi tuned by CV) using xG-blended targets, or use ClubElo with K scaled by margin; include a home-advantage parameter; shrink newly promoted teams toward a promoted-team prior (see soc.preseason_prior).

soc.pace_press.label: Tempo, pressing intensity, possession style
soc.pace_press.mechanism: Pressing intensity, directness and possession share set how many shots occur in total and how open the game is, shifting the total-goals distribution at a given strength level.
soc.pace_press.rationale: Two high-press, high-tempo sides produce more transitions and variance; two low-block sides suppress events. Tempo affects totals and BTTS more than the 1X2 mean. Subtle: possession is partly an outcome of score state (leading teams cede it), so style features must be measured at neutral game state or with a state adjustment.
soc.pace_press.measurement: Compute PPDA, passes per defensive action in opponent half, directness (progressive distance per pass), shots per 90 at score-level state, then form team-pair tempo = f(team_a_pace, team_b_pace, league mean) via a regression of total shots/xG on both teams' style features.

soc.lineups_pit.label: Confirmed lineups timestamped
soc.lineups_pit.mechanism: The confirmed starting eleven reveals who actually plays and which formation; individual-minutes shifts change expected goals by the quality gap between starters and replacements.
soc.lineups_pit.rationale: Confirmed XIs are published about an hour before kickoff, which is the biggest scheduled information shock before the match. Markets that closed or were last traded earlier carry stale team strength. Subtle: the lineup is only knowable at a specific timestamp, so any backtest must use the lineup snapshot visible at the Kalshi decision time, not the final box score.
soc.lineups_pit.measurement: Store lineup snapshots with fetch timestamps; compute lineup value = sum of minute-weighted player ratings (xG+xA contribution, defensive actions, GK PSxG) of the XI vs the season-average XI (soc.xi_strength_delta); flag pregame availability: yes only if snapshot timestamp precedes decision time.

soc.injuries.label: Injuries/suspensions/availability
soc.injuries.mechanism: Absences of key players lower expected team output; the size depends on the player's marginal contribution and on replacement quality.
soc.injuries.rationale: Injury and suspension news reaches the market through press conferences 1-2 days before and last-minute reports on matchday; the information is unevenly priced for second-choice absences and for defenders/goalkeepers. Subtle: 'doubtful' tags are noisy, suspensions are knowable well in advance from card accumulation, and the effect is non-linear (losing one of three key players often costs less than a linear sum).
soc.injuries.measurement: Player-level marginal value = (team xG diff with player minus without, shrunk by minutes) or replacement-level model from player xG/xA/defensive value; sum for out players with a probability weight for doubtful tags from the historical rate that 'doubtful' players start; track suspensions from card counts.

soc.gk.label: Goalkeeper quality and PSxG-GA
soc.gk.mechanism: Goalkeepers convert shot-stopping and distribution skill into goals prevented relative to shot quality faced.
soc.gk.rationale: Post-shot xG minus goals allowed isolates shot-stopping; it is noisy per season and regresses strongly to zero, so naive use overrates hot keepers. Starting-keeper changes (injury, rotation in cups) matter at the match level. Subtle: PSxG includes shot placement credit that mixes shooter skill, so shrinkage is required.
soc.gk.measurement: PSxG minus GA per 90 over >=2 seasons with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (k ~ 15-20 matches-equivalents of shots on target faced), plus sweeping/crossing metrics; apply as an adjustment to the opponent's expected goals when the keeper is confirmed.

soc.player_xg.label: Player shot/xG/xA rates and minutes
soc.player_xg.mechanism: Player-level shot volume, shot quality and expected minutes drive who scores and how much a team loses when a creator or finisher is absent.
soc.player_xg.rationale: Goalscorer and top-scorer markets are driven by shots per 90 times expected minutes times conversion; team-level strength depends on aggregated player contributions. Subtle: finishing over xG regresses, minutes are the key uncertain term (rotation, substitution), and penalty duty inflates raw goals.
soc.player_xg.measurement: Per player: non-penalty xG/90, xA/90, shots/90, touches in box, expected minutes (rolling starts probability x avg minutes), shrink finishing delta toward 0 by shots/(shots+k) with k ~ 100 shots.

soc.set_pieces.label: Set-piece takers and aerial strength
soc.set_pieces.mechanism: Corners, free kicks and long throws form a repeatable chance source dependent on delivery quality, target aerial ability and defensive marking scheme.
soc.set_pieces.rationale: Set-piece xG is a notable share of total xG for some teams and is more persistent than open-play finishing luck. It matters especially for underdogs, whose goals often come from dead balls, and for total-goal rungs where open-play suppression does not apply. Subtle: taker and target availability changes the quantity, and referee-specific foul/pen tendencies influence free-kick volume.
soc.set_pieces.measurement: Set-piece xG for/against per 90, aerial duel win rate of likely starters, corner conversion; compute attack x opponent defence set-piece ratio with shrinkage; adjust for confirmed takers/targets.

soc.rest_travel.label: Rest, congestion, travel, European fixtures
soc.rest_travel.mechanism: Days of rest, density of recent matches and long travel change physical output and rotation propensity.
soc.rest_travel.rationale: Short-rest teams under-perform modestly in running output and are more likely to rotate, especially after midweek European fixtures; this is observable pregame. Subtle: the effect on goals is small and confounded with opponent quality and rotation, so it should be modelled jointly with predicted lineup rotation, not as an independent additive term.
soc.rest_travel.measurement: Days since previous match, matches in last 14/21 days, minutes of starters in last 14 days, travel km and time-zone shift from venue coordinates; estimate via regression on xG difference controlling for ratings.

soc.motivation.label: Competition stakes, relegation/title incentives, rotation
soc.motivation.mechanism: What each team gains from a result (title, European place, survival, nothing) shapes effort, rotation and risk-taking.
soc.motivation.rationale: Late-season fixtures with nothing at stake (dead rubbers) and matches before a more important fixture feature lower intensity and rotated lineups; relegation-threatened and title-chasing teams over-perform ratings that average over the season. Subtle: the effect shows through lineup selection (observable ~1h before) and pushes totals and draws, and the 'motivation' narrative is overpriced by casual flow, so a quantitative leverage measure (soc.stakes_leverage) is needed.
soc.motivation.measurement: Leverage = change in season-outcome probability (title, top-4, relegation) between win/draw/loss from the Monte Carlo season simulation; also next-match importance and distance to next competition; interact with the rotation index.

soc.weather.label: Weather/pitch/altitude
soc.weather.mechanism: Heavy rain, strong wind, extreme heat and altitude change ball control, passing accuracy and stamina, shifting goal expectation and variance.
soc.weather.rationale: Wind and rain reduce passing/shooting quality and tend to lower totals and favour direct teams; extreme heat reduces pressing. Forecasts are knowable pregame (updated through the morning), but the effect is modest and measured across many matches. Subtle: stadium roofs and pitch type (artificial/hybrid) neutralise or alter effects; use kickoff-hour forecast at the stadium coordinates rather than city averages.
soc.weather.measurement: Pull hourly forecast at kickoff +0..2h at venue lat/lon: wind speed/gust, precipitation, temperature, humidity; regress total goals and shot quality on these with league fixed effects; interact with roofed/artificial flags.

soc.referee.label: Referee card/penalty tendencies
soc.referee.mechanism: Referees differ in foul calling, card thresholds, penalty and added-time habits, which shift cards, penalties and game flow.
soc.referee.rationale: Referee assignments are usually announced 2-3 days ahead; penalty rates and card rates are persistent referee traits (after shrinkage) and affect total goals marginally via penalties and set pieces, and cards/booking-based markets strongly. Subtle: sample sizes are small per referee, and the effect on goals is tiny relative to team strength.
soc.referee.measurement: Per referee: fouls, yellows, reds, penalties per match relative to league average, shrunk by matches/(matches+k) with k ~ 20; adjust for team foul propensity (home/away) via a mixed model with referee random effect.

soc.goal_dist.label: Goal-count distributions, correlation
soc.goal_dist.mechanism: The goal-count joint distribution (Poisson with dependence, over-dispersion) converts team strengths into probabilities for results, totals and exact scores.
soc.goal_dist.rationale: Independent Poisson mis-prices low scores and draws; correlated/zero-inflated models fix this, and the distribution of totals is over-dispersed when strength uncertainty is propagated. Subtle: parameter errors in lambda have larger effects on tails (exact score, 4+ goals) than on the mean, so tail rungs are the hardest to price.
soc.goal_dist.measurement: Fit bivariate Poisson or Dixon-Coles with rho, optionally negative-binomial marginals; calibrate via rolling log-loss per outcome and a reliability curve on total goals rungs; propagate lambda uncertainty (soc.ratings_uncertainty).

soc.score_state.label: Game state effects, red cards, substitutions
soc.score_state.mechanism: Scoreline and red cards change risk-taking and possession so the goal rate is state-dependent (trailing teams attack, leading teams sit deep).
soc.score_state.rationale: Used pregame, it supplies the conditional goal-rate multipliers for converting pregame lambdas into period and in-play prices; the ex-ante probability of an early red card and late-state dynamics create fat tails and asymmetry between first half and second half. Subtle: it is not knowable pregame (outcome of play), so only its distribution enters pregame models, and effects are confounded with team quality.
soc.score_state.measurement: Estimate goal-rate multipliers by score-differential and minute bucket (and by numerical player advantage) from play-by-play, normalised by team strength; apply in simulation of match with a minute-level Poisson process.

soc.period_split.label: 1H vs 2H scoring split
soc.period_split.mechanism: Goals are not uniform across halves: the second half has a higher goal rate, with extra added-time and fatigue/substitution effects, and teams differ in start strength.
soc.period_split.rationale: Half-based markets (1H result, 1H total, 1H BTTS) require a split of the full-match lambda; the first-half share is roughly stable at league level (around 45% of goals) but varies by team style, by kickoff and by game-state dynamics. Subtle: first-half draws are very common, so 3-way first-half markets are sharply affected by the draw model.
soc.period_split.measurement: Per team: share of goals scored/conceded in 1H, shrunk to league mean; model lambda_1H = f * lambda_total with f from a regression on team styles; use half-specific Dixon-Coles dependence.

soc.market_odds.label: Closing and live bookmaker odds
soc.market_odds.mechanism: Sharp bookmaker closing odds aggregate lineup news, ratings and sharp money; they are the best single prior and the benchmark any soccer model must be judged against.
soc.market_odds.rationale: Closing odds for 1X2, Asian handicap and totals encode far more information than public stats; the useful signal is the departure between Kalshi and de-vigged sharp price, plus the sharp line's movement. Subtle: free historical data only has opening/closing snapshots, margins differ by book, and draw prices have well-known favourite-longshot distortions.
soc.market_odds.measurement: De-vig (Shin) Pinnacle closing 1X2 and AH/total, fit implied lambdas (soc.implied_lambda_from_lines), compute open-to-close move and compare with the Kalshi quote at the same timestamp.

soc.comp_sim.label: League/cup simulation, tiebreakers, qualification
soc.comp_sim.mechanism: A fixture-by-fixture Monte Carlo of the remaining schedule converts team strength into distributions for title, top-N, relegation and qualification.
soc.comp_sim.rationale: Futures prices depend on the whole path: remaining schedule strength, head-to-head tiebreaks, goal difference, European slots reallocation, and rating uncertainty. Subtle: heavy dependence on how rating uncertainty and drift are modelled (title probabilities are too sharp if team strength is treated as fixed), and tiebreak implementation matters near the cut-off.
soc.comp_sim.measurement: For each remaining fixture, draw goals from the calibrated goal model with team strengths sampled from the posterior (including drift), apply league tiebreak rules, repeat 10k-50k times; report probabilities and standard errors; update after each matchday.

soc.transfers.label: Transfers/manager changes news

soc.transfers.measurement: Net change in squad market value and in position-wise top-XI quality across windows; manager change flag with match-count since; blend prior and in-season ratings with weights depending on matches since change.

soc.home_advantage.label: Home advantage by team, competition and venue type
soc.home_advantage.mechanism: Home advantage works through crowd and referee influence, travel and familiarity, and is a team- and league-specific offset to goal rates (and to draw propensity) rather than a constant.

Subtle: team-specific HFA estimates are noisy and need strong shrinkage to the league-level value.

soc.dixon_coles_low_score.label: Dixon-Coles low-score dependence (rho)
soc.dixon_coles_low_score.mechanism: Independent Poisson misestimates 0-0, 1-0, 0-1 and 1-1 frequencies; the Dixon-Coles tau adjustment re-allocates mass among these cells, changing draw, BTTS-No and exact-score prices.
soc.dixon_coles_low_score.rationale: Because low-score cells carry most of the probability mass for draws and under rungs, even small mis-specification of rho changes draw probability by a point or two and exact-score probabilities by more. Subtle: rho varies by league, era and by total expected goals (stronger when lambdas are low); time-decay matters and it is easily over-fit.
soc.dixon_coles_low_score.measurement: Maximum likelihood rho in a Dixon-Coles model with exponential time decay, estimated per league on 3+ seasons; check the empirical vs fitted frequencies for 0-0, 1-0, 0-1, 1-1 conditional on lambda tertiles; alternative: bivariate Poisson with covariance parameter.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.label: Opponent- and venue-adjusted xG attack/defence ratings
soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.mechanism: A joint regression of per-match xG on team attack, opposition defence and home effects strips schedule effects so each team's rating reflects its quality, not its fixtures.
soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.rationale: Raw xG averages mix quality with opposition strength and with game state. A ridge/hierarchical model identifies attack and defence parameters with shrinkage that handles sparse samples and rotates through league structure. Subtle: cross-league comparisons need linking data, and using season-end ratings in a backtest leaks future results.

soc.finishing_regression.label: Finishing over/under-performance vs xG (regression to mean)
soc.finishing_regression.mechanism: Realised goals minus xG for a team or player is mostly noise with a small persistent skill component, so it regresses toward zero; ratings built on goals over-weight luck.
soc.finishing_regression.rationale: Teams on hot finishing streaks are overrated by goal-based models and sometimes by markets, whereas the persistent part (elite finishers) is small and mostly at player level. Subtle: shot placement/volume and psxG-based measures capture some skill; the shrinkage constant must be estimated, not guessed; penalty goals should be excluded.

soc.keeper_shot_stopping_regression.label: Goalkeeper save over/under-performance regression
soc.keeper_shot_stopping_regression.mechanism: PSxG minus goals conceded is noisy but contains a small persistent component, so extreme keeper form should be shrunk heavily before projecting forward.
soc.keeper_shot_stopping_regression.rationale: A keeper on a hot run depresses a team's observed goals-against beyond xG-against; market and naive models extrapolate that, causing mispricing of under rungs and clean-sheet markets. soc.award_voting_narrative.measurement: Features: goals+assists, team trophies, tournament result, media-share proxies; fit conditional-logit on past winners/finalists with shrinkage; update with trophy simulations.
free_sources: football-data.org v4 free tier (fixtures, standings, scorers)
Wikipedia competition pages (format, tiebreakers, points deductions, qualification slots)
Awarding bodies' published criteria and past winners (e.g., PFA, FWA, Ballon d'Or lists)

soc.official_announcement_signals.label: Governance/announcement calendar for off-field markets
soc.official_announcement_signals.mechanism: Off-field outcomes (host selection, managers, transfers, rule changes) are determined by committees and negotiations with timelines and pre-announced dates, not by on-pitch performance.
soc.official_announcement_signals.rationale: Prices should follow the information schedule: evaluation reports, shortlists, vote dates, leaks from credible reporters. Base rates for how often rumours convert are the main quantitative input. Subtle: leaks are strategic, and markets can be driven by rumour; no systematic model exists, so treat these as hypotheses needing manual judgement.
soc.official_announcement_signals.measurement: Event calendar with decision dates, base rates of leak-to-confirmation conversion by source tier, time-to-event decay; map contract wording to formal announcement.
free_sources: Wikipedia competition pages (format, tiebreakers, points deductions, qualification slots)
UEFA.com and FIFA.com regulations and coefficient pages (public)
Official federation/club announcement pages (public)

soc.paired_team_correlation.label: Correlation of two teams' season outcomes
soc.paired_team_correlation.mechanism: Head-to-head and joint markets for two teams depend on correlated outcomes (they play each other, share schedule and competition) so independence is wrong.
soc.paired_team_correlation.rationale: In a head-to-head 'who finishes higher' market, the direct matches and shared rating uncertainty create dependence; simulating both teams within one league sim captures it, while marginal probabilities do not. Subtle: dependence is via shared schedule and shared uncertainty about league strength.
soc.paired_team_correlation.measurement: Use the joint Monte Carlo output to compute P(rank_A < rank_B), points difference distributions; sensitivity to rating uncertainty.
free_sources: football-data.co.uk historical odds CSVs (results, shots, corners, cards, referee, opening/closing odds)
openfootball (github.com/openfootball) fixtures and results

soc.points_total_distribution.label: Distribution of a team's final points
soc.points_total_distribution.mechanism: Points-total and points-margin markets need the whole distribution (variance and skew) of a team's final points, not just the expectation.
soc.points_total_distribution.rationale: Variance depends on goal-model calibration, rating uncertainty and correlation among matches; neglecting strength uncertainty produces over-tight distributions and mis-prices tails and margins. Subtle: draws are the main driver of point variance and are hard to price.
soc.points_total_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo of remaining fixtures with strength sampled from the posterior; report quantiles and tail probabilities; calibrate against historical final points vs preseason forecasts.
free_sources: football-data.co.uk historical odds CSVs (results, shots, corners, cards, referee, opening/closing odds)
openfootball (github.com/openfootball) fixtures and results
football-data.org v4 free tier (fixtures, standings, scorers)

soc.ratings_uncertainty.label: Rating uncertainty and strength drift
soc.ratings_uncertainty.mechanism: Team strength is a moving, uncertain quantity; treating it as a known constant makes season-long and tail probabilities too extreme.
soc.ratings_uncertainty.rationale: Posterior uncertainty about a team's attack/defence is a first-order driver of futures probabilities and of tail rungs; strengths drift with form, injuries and tactical change. Subtle: a state-space model (random walk strength) is more principled than a fixed decay but harder to estimate.
soc.ratings_uncertainty.measurement: Estimate strength posterior covariance from Bayesian/state-space model (random-walk variance tuned by CV); propagate samples into simulation; compare calibration of title probabilities historically.
free_sources: ClubElo API (api.clubelo.com/<date> and /<club>)
football-data.co.uk historical odds CSVs (results, shots, corners, cards, referee, opening/closing odds)
FBref match/team/player tables (Opta-sourced xG, shots, possession, passing)

soc.league_baseline_environment.label: League/season baseline goal and draw environment
soc.league_baseline_environment.mechanism: League-season baselines (goals per match, home share, draw rate, red-card frequency) set the prior scale of all lambdas and shift every total/draw market.
soc.league_baseline_environment.rationale: Goal rates differ across leagues and drift across seasons and months (more late goals, VAR effects); mixing leagues without baselines mis-calibrates totals. Subtle: early-season baselines are small samples; rule changes (added time) shift them.
soc.league_baseline_environment.measurement: League-season rolling goals/match, home goal share, draw rate with shrinkage to previous seasons; include as intercepts in Poisson models.
free_sources: football-data.co.uk historical odds CSVs (results, shots, corners, cards, referee, opening/closing odds)
FBref match/team/player tables (Opta-sourced xG, shots, possession, passing)
football-data.org v4 free tier (fixtures, standings, scorers)

soc.score_effects_adjusted_xg.label: Game-state-adjusted xG
soc.score_effects_adjusted_xg.mechanism: Leading teams concede more shots but of lower quality and trailing teams shoot more; adjusting xG by game state recovers the neutral-state strength.
soc.score_effects_adjusted_xg.rationale: A team that was often ahead has deflated attacking xG and inflated xG against, misleading raw averages. Adjustment is important for teams with extreme results and for ratings across weak/strong schedules. Subtle: state adjustment requires minute-level shot data; free sources cover limited seasons.
soc.score_effects_adjusted_xg.measurement: Weight each shot's xG by multipliers per score-differential bin estimated from league data (or restrict to level-state minutes); recompute rolling team xG for/against.
free_sources: StatsBomb open data (github.com/statsbomb/open-data, selected competitions)
FBref match/team/player tables (Opta-sourced xG, shots, possession, passing)
Understat league and player pages (shot-level xG, xGChain)

soc.favourite_longshot_bias.label: Favourite-longshot and draw-price distortions
soc.favourite_longshot_bias.mechanism: Prices of long-shot outcomes (big underdog wins, exact scores) are systematically biased relative to frequencies, and draws are priced differently from sides.
soc.favourite_longshot_bias.rationale: Calibration of sharp prices by probability bucket reveals persistent distortions: retail demand inflates long-shot prices, and thin markets inherit them. The correction depends on the de-vig method and bucket; wide exact-score ladders have the greatest distortion. Subtle: apparent bias can be vig-removal error; estimate on out-of-sample data.
soc.favourite_longshot_bias.measurement: Calibration curves of de-vigged probabilities by bucket on historical closing odds (football-data.co.uk) and results; fit power/Shin parameters; apply correction when comparing Kalshi prices to model.
free_sources: football-data.co.uk historical odds CSVs (results, shots, corners, cards, referee, opening/closing odds)
Betfair Exchange historical data (data.betfair.com basic plan)

m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series
m.quote_history.mechanism: Prices aggregate dispersed information; the path of the quote (and its drift toward kickoff) reveals when informed flow arrives and how stale an early quote is.
m.quote_history.rationale: A resting Kalshi quote hours before kickoff is partly stale: team news, injury and line moves at sharp books arrive in bursts, and Kalshi liquidity is thin so quotes can lag. The quote path also defines the realistic entry price (not a mid that was never tradable). Subtle: last-trade can be far from the executable bid/ask, and closing-quote efficiency is a benchmark rather than a given.
m.quote_history.measurement: Snapshot bid/ask/mid/last at fixed horizons (T-24h, T-6h, T-1h, T-10m, close); compute spread, time since last trade, and signed drift vs the sharp-book de-vigged price at the same timestamp. Never use post-start quotes for pregame features.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks)

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Executable size at each price level, not the mid, determines how much edge can be captured and what slippage costs.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: A model edge of two cents is worthless if depth at the touch is a handful of contracts; wide spreads on long-shot rungs mean the quoted probability is mostly spread. Depth also signals whether a market maker is active (tight, refreshed quotes) or the book is abandoned (stale quotes that will be picked off when news lands).
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Record top-5 level price/size per side, cumulative depth within 1/2/5 cents of mid, spread in cents and as fraction of price; compute expected fill price for a target size.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks)

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Traded volume and open interest proxy how much information and capital has been committed, hence how trustworthy the price is.
m.volume_oi.rationale: High-volume rungs are usually closer to sharp consensus; thin rungs deviate and can be mispriced but are also costly to trade. Volume spikes near the news window reveal when informed trading happens. Subtle: volume is cumulative by market and cannot be compared across markets with different contract caps without normalising.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Per market: cumulative volume, OI, volume in the last hour before close, volume rank within the family; log-scale features and ratios to family median.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks)

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Adjacent threshold markets (over 1.5/2.5/3.5 goals, handicap steps) must form a monotone cumulative distribution; violations or kinks expose mispriced rungs and the implied distribution of the underlying count.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Each rung is priced separately by different participants, so the implied pmf (differences between adjacent cumulative prices) can go negative or be implausibly lumpy. Fitting a smooth parametric distribution across rungs and trading the residual is a market-structure edge that does not depend on a view about the teams. Subtle: push rules and integer vs half-point lines change which rung differences are legitimate.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Collect all rungs of an event at one timestamp; check monotonicity of cumulative prices; fit a constrained distribution (bivariate Poisson / negative binomial for goals) by least squares on mid prices and record per-rung residuals and implied pmf.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks)

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: Settlement is the realised label; the exact settled value and timestamp (not the box-score) is what pays.
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Labels must be taken from Kalshi's recorded settlement, not re-derived from a stats site: edge cases (extra time, abandoned matches, retirements, source corrections after the fact) can make the settled value differ from the intuitive result. It is never a pregame feature but is the ground truth for backtests and for measuring how often wording edge cases occur.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Join each market to its settled result/value and settlement time; flag markets whose settled value disagrees with an independently computed result as wording/void cases.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks); settled market fields (result, settlement_value, settlement_ts)

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording
m.rules_text.mechanism: Wording fixes the event: regulation time vs extra time/penalties, treatment of abandoned or postponed matches, source of record, and what a draw does to two-way markets.
m.rules_text.rationale: The same colloquial question ('will X win', 'over 2.5 goals') settles differently under different wording: knockout ties can resolve in regulation only, advancement markets include ET/penalties, and abandoned matches may void or settle on the score at abandonment. Mis-reading the rule destroys an apparent edge. Subtle: wording can change between series/seasons so it must be versioned and parsed, not assumed.
m.rules_text.measurement: Store rules text with a version hash at each fetch; parse into flags (regulation_only, includes_ET, includes_pens, void_if_abandoned, void_if_retired, min_games_required, source_of_record) and use them as hard filters/feature switches.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks); market rules_primary / rules_secondary fields

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook/exchange reference prices
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp external prices are an information-rich prior; a Kalshi price that disagrees with the de-vigged sharp close either carries a stale quote or genuine information.
m.external_lines.rationale: The sharp closing line is the best-known single predictor in most sports markets, so any model must clear it, and its de-vigging method matters (proportional vs Shin vs power) especially for 3-way markets and long-shots. Subtle: timestamps must be matched; using a closing price against an earlier Kalshi quote overstates edge (look-ahead), and free historical files only give open/close snapshots.
m.external_lines.measurement: De-vig each external quote (Shin for 3-way/long-shot-heavy sets, power for two-way), timestamp-match to the Kalshi quote, compute the Kalshi minus sharp probability difference and its sign persistence.
free_sources: football-data.co.uk historical odds CSVs (Bet365, Pinnacle, Betfair exchange columns; opening and closing)
Betfair Exchange historical data (data.betfair.com basic plan)

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules
m.fees.mechanism: Fees reduce realised edge nonlinearly in price (larger relative drag near 50c and for small expected edges), so the net-of-fee probability threshold differs by rung.
m.fees.rationale: A model edge below the fee-plus-spread hurdle is not tradable; the hurdle depends on price level and on maker vs taker. Fee rules change over time so a historical backtest must apply the schedule in force on the trade date. It does not predict the outcome but determines which model edges are monetisable.
m.fees.measurement: Implement fee(price, size, role, date) from the schedule; compute net edge = model_p minus price minus fee/contract minus half-spread; evaluate decisions on net edge.
free_sources: Kalshi fee schedule PDF / help center (kalshi.com/fee-schedule)

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: The lifecycle (open, close before start, halts, postponement, early settlement) controls when information can still be traded on and which markets get voided or re-opened.
m.lifecycle.rationale: Markets that close at kickoff block any in-play correction; a postponement or abandonment can leave capital tied up or void the contract. Close-time vs scheduled kickoff must be checked per market since delays can change what a pregame quote means.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Log status transitions with timestamps; compute minutes between last tradable quote and event start; flag postponements, delays >30 min, halts and re-opens.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks); market status/open_time/close_time/expiration fields

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Calibration by rung exposes systematic mispricing at specific strikes (e.g. favourite-longshot bias, popular round numbers) independent of any team model.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: Ladders attract round-number and narrative bias: some rungs settle YES more often than priced, others less. The frequency table is a prior and a calibration check for the model, not a causal input; it needs enough settled history per family/strike and a shrinkage rule to avoid chasing noise.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: For each family and strike bucket: realised YES rate minus average de-vigged pre-close price, with Wilson intervals; shrink toward zero by n/(n+k).
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks) settled history (result by strike per family)

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time)
m.trade_tape.mechanism: Trade prints with taker side show where aggressive flow went, how fast the price moves after trades (impact) and what fills were realistically achievable.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Order-flow imbalance before the news window can foreshadow lineup/injury information; trade size distribution separates informed from retail flow; post-trade price reversion measures adverse selection. Subtle: public tape lacks participant identity, so flow signals are noisy and must be validated out of sample.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Compute signed volume imbalance (taker side), VWAP vs mid, price impact over the next 1/5/30 minutes, trade count and size quantiles per market per hour.
free_sources: Kalshi public market data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks) /markets/trades endpoint

soc.offfield_base_rate.label: Reference-class base rates for soccer appointments, transfers and hosts
soc.offfield_base_rate.mechanism: Announcement markets are priced from historical frequency conditional on calendar windows.
soc.offfield_base_rate.rationale: Manager, transfer and host markets depend on windows (transfer deadlines, tournament cycles) and club circumstances, which a base-rate model captures better than game data.
soc.offfield_base_rate.measurement: Event counts per window and club state (position in table, tenure) from transfer and manager-change archives, shrunk, with announcement timestamps.
free_sources: Transfermarkt public pages (check terms)
Football-data.co.uk team results as context

soc.award_vote_distribution.label: Award vote-share distribution (Ballon d'Or, golden boot, panel awards)
soc.award_vote_distribution.mechanism: Panel awards are decided by vote shares driven by team success and narrative.
soc.award_vote_distribution.rationale: Award markets need a distribution across candidates: production to date, team trophies and media narrative interact; prior-year voting predicts next year's ranking. Subtle: tournament years shift weight to international performance.
soc.award_vote_distribution.measurement: Fit a conditional-logit on historical winners with production, team success and prior-vote features; output probabilities per candidate with uncertainty.
free_sources: FBref player production tables
Public voting results archives

soc.player_shot_share.label: Player shot and shot-on-target share of team volume
soc.player_shot_share.mechanism: A player's shots are a share of team shots driven by role, set-piece duty and position in the attack.
soc.player_shot_share.rationale: Shots, shots-on-target and goalscorer markets convert team volume into player volume through share; share is stable within a role but jumps when a teammate is absent or a penalty taker changes. Subtle: share must be measured per minute played and net of penalties.
soc.player_shot_share.measurement: Shots and SOT per 90 and share of team shots, split open play / set pieces / penalties, with minutes-weighted shrinkage toward the position mean; recompute with the confirmed lineup.
free_sources: FBref player shooting tables (Opta-sourced)
football-data.co.uk team shots and shots on target (team level)

soc.opp_shot_profile_by_zone.label: Opponent shots and chances conceded by zone and position
soc.opp_shot_profile_by_zone.mechanism: Defences concede shots in specific zones and to specific positions; a striker's chances depend on where the opponent is weak.
soc.opp_shot_profile_by_zone.rationale: A defence that concedes wide crosses favours target men; one that concedes through-balls favours runners. Matching player shot zones to the opponent's conceded zones sharpens player props beyond team strength.
soc.opp_shot_profile_by_zone.measurement: Shots and xG conceded per 90 by zone and by attacker position, opponent-adjusted, shrunk by matches played.
free_sources: FBref team shot-creation and conceded tables
Understat shot location data (check terms)

soc.keeper_workload.label: Expected shots-on-target faced by the goalkeeper
soc.keeper_workload.mechanism: Saves are shots on target faced times save probability.
soc.keeper_workload.rationale: Goalkeeper saves markets are a count driven by opponent shot volume and quality and the keeper's own stopping skill, shrunk heavily because save percentage is noisy.
soc.keeper_workload.measurement: Expected SOT faced from both teams' shot-on-target generation and game state; multiply by shrunk save probability (PSxG-based) to price the count distribution.
free_sources: football-data.co.uk team shots on target (HST/AST)
FBref goalkeeper tables

game_side.mechanism: Match-side markets (1X2, two-way, handicap, exact score, first-half and second-half results) are settled by the joint goal difference in a defined window. The mechanism is a latent attack/defence strength per team, adjusted for opponent and venue, converted to a goal distribution with low-score dependence, then modified by who plays (confirmed XI), rest/rotation, motivation and a game-state process. The market's sharp price carries much of this information, so the incremental inputs are those that arrive late or are mispriced (lineups, rotation, stakes) plus market-structure details.
game_side.target: Win/draw/loss or goal-difference threshold in regulation (or a half), as defined in the rules text.

inputs.why: Opponent- and venue-adjusted xG attack/defence is the base strength estimate for the goal-difference distribution.
Elo/Dixon-Coles ratings provide the long-memory prior that stabilises noisy xG samples.
Team/league-specific home offset shifts both goal rates and draw probabilities.
Low-score dependence sets draw and 1-0/0-1 cells that dominate side markets.
Confirmed lineup quality vs typical XI converts team news into a strength adjustment.
Predicting rotation before the XI release gives an early signal when quotes are stale.
Key absences and suspensions known days ahead shift expected goal difference.
Match importance for each side alters effort, rotation and draw acceptability.
Team-pair draw tendency beyond Poisson baselines for 3-way prices.
Past finishing over-performance should be shrunk, not extrapolated.
De-vigged sharp closing odds are the benchmark prior any model must beat.
Quote path shows when the Kalshi price last absorbed team news.
Wording decides regulation-only vs advancement and abandonment/void handling.
Raw and state-adjusted team xG for/against feeds the adjusted rating and sanity-checks goal-based ratings.
Timestamped confirmed XI: only lineups visible before the decision time may be used, and quotes before release are stale.
Qualitative stakes (title, survival, cup priority) that the leverage index quantifies.
Days of rest and travel feed fatigue and rotation expectations for both sides.
Tactical matchup residual visible once the XI is out.
Derbies compress goal margins and raise cards, nudging results toward draws.
Long trips matter in continental cups and tournaments, mostly for the away side.
Depth at the touch decides whether any model edge is executable.

interactions.hypothesis: A rating built on full-strength XIs should be reduced in proportion to the confirmed XI shortfall; the interaction is multiplicative in the attack/defence components, not additive.
Low-leverage matches raise rotation probability, so the expected-XI shift is larger exactly when stakes are low and the effect on the draw probability is largest.
Strong home edge moves mass from draw to home win in evenly matched sides; weak-HFA venues (neutral, empty stadium) raise draw share.
The edge from comparing a model with sharp odds depends on correcting favourite-longshot and draw-price distortions, otherwise the apparent gap is a de-vig artefact.
Quote adaptation after lineup release measures how stale pre-XI quotes were and when informed flow arrives.

game_total.mechanism: Total-goal style markets (over/under rungs, team totals, BTTS, first-half totals) are determined by the sum of two correlated count processes. The mechanism is each team's expected goals (attack vs opponent defence), a dependence structure that handles low scores, a tempo/openness factor from both teams' styles, weather, referee/penalty tendencies and lineup quality, and game-state feedback (leading teams sit deep). Strength uncertainty fattens tails so high rungs are more probable than a plain Poisson implies.
game_total.target: Total goals (or team total / both-score events) in the contract's time window relative to a strike.

Set-piece xG is a persistent goal source for underdogs and in cagey games.
League-season goal baseline anchors the intercept of all lambdas.

Cross-rung consistency exposes mispriced thresholds.
Historical realised frequency per rung checks calibration.
Open-play and set-piece xG for/against by team is the raw material of the lambdas.
Shot volume by game state gives tempo/volume cross-check to xG.
Corner volume reflects wing play and territorial pressure, correlated with totals.
Card/foul tempo and red-card risk change game flow and variance.
Attacking vs defensive formations change openness.
Confirmed lineups give the actual attack/defence units.
Rest and congestion alter intensity and rotation.
State-adjusted xG removes the bias of being ahead/behind in sampled matches.
VAR reviews shift disallowed goals/penalties and stoppage time.
Longer added time raises late-goal chances.
Liquidity by rung indicates which rungs are efficiently priced.
Realised totals for calibration by rung.

interactions.hypothesis: Two high-tempo teams raise total xG more than the sum of main effects, so tempo scales both teams' lambdas rather than adding a constant.
Wind/rain hurt possession-based high-press sides more than direct teams, so the weather effect on totals depends on style.
Over-dispersion and rho shape the whole ladder; a mis-specified distribution creates systematic residuals that look like per-rung mispricing.
Keeper changes interact with outfield rotation: a weaker defence in front of a weaker keeper raises opponent goal expectation convexly.

season_outcome.mechanism: Season-outcome futures (title, top-N, relegation, qualification, advancement, outright, host, trophies) are the outcome of a stochastic tournament: remaining fixtures are simulated from team strengths with uncertainty and drift, then tiebreak and slot rules are applied. The mechanism is the aggregate of many match outcomes, so value comes from correct rating uncertainty, schedule strength, rule details, squad depth and injuries, and correlation across teams. Long-horizon prices embed more information drift than match prices, so the underlying rating prior and rule parsing matter most.
season_outcome.target: Final league position/qualification/advancement or trophy outcome, as defined by competition rules and the contract wording.

inputs.why: Fixture-by-fixture Monte Carlo is the structural engine that maps strengths to season outcomes.
Strength posterior and drift determine tail probabilities and avoid over-sharp futures.
Order, venues and rival fixtures shift expected points among equal-rated teams.
Tiebreak order and slot allocation decide close cut-offs.
Sanctions shift points irrespective of on-pitch strength.
Depth affects strength under injuries and congestion over the horizon.
Current long-term absences adjust remaining-season strength.
Window moves and manager changes update stale ratings.
Early-season futures lean on priors until matches accumulate.
Multi-competition load links separate futures for the same team.
Leverage tells which remaining fixtures matter for the cut-off.
Sharp futures and match prices are strong priors for ratings.
Contract wording defines the exact qualifying outcome (including playoff/ET handling).
Top-N rungs must be consistent with winner and relegation probabilities.
xG-based ratings are less noisy than points for long-horizon strength.
Elo/Dixon-Coles ratings are the strength input to the simulation.
Late-season incentives change effort and rotation in simulated fixtures.
Postponed/abandoned fixtures reshuffle the schedule and can void markets.
Knockout advancement beyond 90 minutes includes shootouts.
Advancement-wording markets include extra time and penalties.
Aggregate state in two-legged ties.

interactions.hypothesis: Propagating strength uncertainty into the simulation flattens title/relegation probabilities relative to fixed-strength sims; the flattening is largest for the favourites and near the cut.
Schedule matters most when the table is tight and tiebreaks (H2H, GD) decide; the interaction is non-linear near cut-off.
Teams in multiple competitions with thin squads lose more strength in the league run-in, so depth interacts with cup progression.
A deduction changes who reaches a tiebreak and which tiebreak applies, creating non-additive effects in relegation and qualification markets.

season_stat.mechanism: Season-stat markets (team points, points margin, player total, season leader) settle on an accumulated count over remaining fixtures. The mechanism is a sum of match-level processes (points or goals) with strength uncertainty, rotation and injury risk, and tie-break or rounding rules. Player stats additionally depend on minutes, role, penalty duty and finishing luck regression; team points depend on schedule strength and draw variance.
season_stat.target: A season-end count (points, goals, assists, margin) relative to a threshold or relative to another entity.

inputs.why: Full distribution (variance, skew) of points for threshold and margin markets.
Remaining opponents and venues set expected additional points.
Posterior strength uncertainty widens the distribution of totals.
Current tally, minutes and remaining fixtures set player race outcomes.
Player shot volume and shot quality produce expected remaining goals/assists.
Expected minutes are the largest uncertainty for player counting stats.
Penalty duty adds high-xG chances for scoring totals.
Observed over-performance should be shrunk toward xG-implied production.
Injury hazard truncates player and team output.
Draw variance drives dispersion of points totals.
Defines what is counted (league only, own goals, tie-break rules).
Threshold ladder must be consistent with distribution.
Team-level xG is the strength basis for expected points.
Dead-rubber effects on late-season points.

player_shots_saves_props.label: Soccer player shots, shots on target and goalkeeper saves
player_shots_saves_props.target: A player's shot or shot-on-target count, or a goalkeeper's saves, relative to a threshold.
player_shots_saves_props.mechanism: Shot counts are team shot volume times the player's share times minutes, shaped by game state (trailing teams shoot more) and the opponent's block and press profile. Goalkeeper saves are the opponent's shots on target times the keeper's save probability, which is noisy and must be shrunk. Both are over-dispersed counts and depend on the confirmed lineup.

inputs.why: Team shots and SOT for and against set the volume to be shared.
Player share by role converts team volume to player volume.
Confirmed lineup fixes who plays and in which role.
Expected minutes and substitution risk scale every shot and save count.
Expected SOT faced is the keeper-saves volume.
Keeper quality (PSxG minus goals allowed) shrunk toward average.
Pressing and tempo change shot volume.
Trailing teams shoot more; leading teams concede more shots.
Opponent block and zone profile changes shot conversion to SOT.
Formation changes who takes shots.

interactions.hypothesis: Shot volume is convex in expected deficit: heavy underdogs concede many shots while taking few, changing both player and keeper counts.
Keeper saves depend on volume times shrunk skill; volume dominates unless skill is extreme.
A teammate's absence raises shot share in a position-specific way.

corners_and_cards_team_events.label: Soccer corners, cards and fouls
corners_and_cards_team_events.target: Count of corners, cards or fouls in a match relative to a threshold.
corners_and_cards_team_events.mechanism: Corners follow territorial pressure, wing play and blocked shots; cards and fouls follow referee tendencies, derby intensity, tackle volume and score state. Both are over-dispersed counts that correlate with possession and game state. The referee appointment is announced days ahead and is the single most informative card input.

inputs.why: Team corners for and against per 90, opponent-adjusted, are the base rate.
Team and player foul and card rates are the base of card markets.
Referee card and penalty tendencies are the largest known card driver and are published in advance.
Pressing intensity creates fouls and turnovers.
Wide formations generate corners and crosses.
Derbies raise fouls and cards.
High-stakes matches raise cards.
Trailing teams earn corners; late leads add time-wasting cards.
Set-piece attack versus defence shifts corner-to-goal conversion.
VAR reviews add stoppage and cards.
Added time lengthens the window for corners and cards.

interactions.hypothesis: A card-happy referee in a derby compounds the baseline.
Corners cluster in the trailing team's spell, so the mean is conditional on the expected score path.
